steps.body: Real floor plans often need THREE or more pieces: a main room, an extension, maybe a nook. The rule scales up perfectly — identify every piece's shape, compute each area, then combine with add or subtract as each piece demands. A main room (12×8=96) plus an extension (4×5=20) plus a triangular reading nook (1/2×4×3=6) totals **122**.

widget.prompt: A floor plan has two rectangular rooms: 7×4 and 3×6. What is the total floor area?

choices.label: 28 square units
choices.feedback: 28 is only the first room (7×4), leaving out the second. Add both: 28 + 18 = 46.

choices.label: 504 square units
choices.feedback: 504 multiplies the two room-areas together. Combine separate rooms by ADDING: 28 + 18 = 46.

predict.prompt: Two rooms, 7 × 4 and 3 × 6. Can you total the floor by combining dimensions first — (7 + 3) × (4 + 6)?
predict.reveal: Gluing the rooms doesn't build a 10 × 10 square — that phantom square holds 100, more than double the truth. Each room's area is computed on its own — 28 and 18 — and only the AREAS are added: 46.

explanationVariants: Compute each piece by its own shape's formula, then add.

widget.prompt: A floor plan has a 6×5 rectangular room plus a triangular bay window (base 6, height 2). What is the total area?

choices.label: 42 square units
choices.feedback: 42 treats the bay window like a rectangle (6×2=12, plus 30=42). It's a TRIANGLE: 1/2×6×2=6, giving 30+6=36.

choices.label: 30 square units
choices.feedback: 30 is only the main room, forgetting the bay window. Add it: 30 + 6 = 36.

steps.body: The ORDER you add pieces never changes the total — 96 + 20 + 6 gives the same result as 20 + 6 + 96. Group however makes the arithmetic easiest, especially when a subtraction is mixed in: compute every piece first, THEN combine with the correct signs (+ for attached, − for removed).

explanationVariants: Compute each piece, then add all three: 41.

widget.prompt: A floor plan has three rectangular sections: 5×4, 3×3, and 2×6. What is the total area?

choices.label: 29 square units
choices.feedback: 29 leaves out one section — check: 20 + 9 = 29, missing the 2×6 piece (12). Full total: 20+9+12 = 41.

choices.label: 2160 square units
choices.feedback: 2160 multiplies all three areas together. Combine separate sections by ADDING: 20+9+12 = 41.

steps.body: Mixed operations: subtract the pool, add the shed.

widget.prompt: A 15×10 yard has a triangular pool (base 4, height 3) dug OUT of it, and a 3×3 shed built onto the remaining space. What is the total usable area (yard minus pool, plus shed)?

choices.label: 141 square units
choices.feedback: 141 subtracts the shed instead of adding it. The shed is BUILT ON (add); the pool is DUG OUT (subtract): 150 − 6 + 9 = 153.

choices.label: 165 square units
choices.feedback: 165 adds the pool instead of subtracting it. A dug-out pool REMOVES area: 150 − 6 + 9 = 153.

explanationVariants: (96 + 20) + 6 = 122, and 96 + (20 + 6) = 122 — same total, regardless of grouping.
Addition can be grouped any way without changing the sum.

widget.prompt: For the three-piece floor plan (96 + 20 + 6 = 122), does grouping the addition differently — (20 + 6) + 96 instead — change the total?

options.label: No — addition gives the same total regardless of grouping
Yes — you must add pieces in the exact order given
options.feedback: Addition is flexible — you can group pieces in whatever order makes the arithmetic easiest, and the total stays 122.

options.label: It depends on which piece is the triangle
options.feedback: The shape identity affects each piece's OWN formula, but once you have each area, adding them in any order gives 122.

hints: A different triangular notch is CUT AWAY (subtract): 1/2×3×2=3.
explanationVariants: 60 + 16 + 6 − 3 = 79 — two rectangles and a nook add, while the cut-away notch subtracts.
Compute each of the four pieces separately, then combine with the right signs: 79.

widget.prompt: A floor plan has: a 10×6 rectangle, a 4×4 rectangle (both added), a triangular nook added (base 4, height 3), and a triangular notch cut away (base 3, height 2). What is the total area?

choices.label: 85 square units
choices.feedback: 85 adds the notch instead of subtracting it (60+16+6+3). The notch is CUT AWAY: 60+16+6−3 = 79.

choices.label: 76 square units
choices.feedback: 76 forgets the added nook's area. Include all four pieces with correct signs: 60+16+6−3 = 79.

steps.body: Every piece, its own formula, combined correctly.
takeaways: Multi-piece figures scale the same rule: identify each piece's shape, compute separately.
Addition can be grouped any way without changing the total.
Track which pieces ADD (attached) and which SUBTRACT (cut away) before combining.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Compute every piece, THEN combine with the right sign.** Two added rectangles (5×3=15 and 2×4=8) plus one subtracted triangle (1/2×2×2=2): 15 + 8 − 2 = 21.

explanationVariants: Add the two rectangles, then subtract the cut-away triangle: 21.

widget.prompt: A figure has two added rectangles (5×3 and 2×4) and one subtracted triangle (base 2, height 2). What is the total area?

choices.label: 25 square units
choices.feedback: 25 adds the triangle instead of subtracting it (15+8+2). It's cut away: 15+8−2 = 21.

choices.label: 13 square units
choices.feedback: 13 forgets one of the rectangles. Include all three pieces with correct signs: 15+8−2 = 21.
